title: Agreement between subject and verb 3
subtitle: the news is / the criteria are
summary: Get the verb right after nouns that only look plural (news, politics, data) and after measurements, percentages and fractions.

lesson.heading: Nouns that are usually plural
lesson.text: Some nouns are normally plural and take a plural verb: **belongings, clothes, congratulations, earnings, goods, outskirts, overheads, particulars** (= information), **premises** (= building), **riches, savings, stairs, surroundings, thanks**.

examples.text: The company's earnings **have** increased for the last five years.
The coastal surroundings of the village **are** particularly attractive.

lesson.heading: police, people, staff, whereabouts
lesson.text: **Police** and **people** always take a plural verb, and **staff** usually does. **Whereabouts** can go with either a singular or a plural verb.

examples.text: Police **believe** that Thomas is in Brazil, although his exact whereabouts **are** / **is** unknown.
Staff **say** that the new computer system has led to greater levels of stress in their work.

lesson.heading: data and media, but criteria and phenomena
lesson.text: **Data** and **media** (= newspapers, television, etc.) are plural forms (singular *datum, medium*) but are commonly used with a singular verb; in formal contexts such as academic writing a plural verb is preferred. **Criteria** and **phenomena** (singular *criterion, phenomenon*), however, are always plural.

examples.text: All the data **is** available for public inspection.
examples.note: or ... are available ... in formal writing

examples.text: I agree that the criteria **are** not of equal importance.
Phenomena such as sun spots **have** puzzled scientists for centuries.

lesson.heading: Uncountable nouns ending in -s
lesson.text: Some uncountable nouns always end in *-s* and look plural, but as the subject they take a singular verb: **news; means** (= method or money); **economics, linguistics, mathematics, phonetics, physics, politics, statistics, athletics, gymnastics, diabetes, measles, rabies**.

examples.text: The news from the Middle East **seems** very encouraging.
Measles **has** killed a large number of children in the Nagola region.
Contact us by whatever means **is** most convenient for you: phone, email or fax.

lesson.heading: The academic subject or the everyday meaning?

left.label: Academic subject - singular verb
examples: Economics **has** only recently been recognised as a scientific study.

right.label: General use - plural verb
examples: Her politics **are** bordering on the fascist.
Statistics **are** able to prove anything you want them to.
The economics behind their policies **are** unreasonable.

lesson.note: politics = political beliefs; statistics = numerical information; economics = the financial system.

lesson.heading: Measurements, amounts and quantities
lesson.text: With a phrase referring to a measurement, amount or quantity we usually prefer a singular verb - and a singular verb **must** be used when the complement is a singular noun phrase such as *a long time*.

examples.text: Only three metres **separates** the runners in first and second places.
Three hours **seems** a long time to take on the homework.

lesson.heading: Percentages and fractions
lesson.text: When the first noun in a complex subject is a percentage or a fraction, the verb agrees with the noun **closest** to it. And where the noun can be thought of either as one unit or as a collection of individuals, either verb is possible.

examples.text: An inflation rate of only 2% **makes** a difference to exports.
examples.note: the verb agrees with the main noun, rate

examples.text: About 50% / half of the houses **need** major repairs.
examples.note: the verb agrees with the closest noun, houses

examples.text: Some 80% of the electorate **is** expected to vote.

lesson.text: An *-s* on the end is no proof of a plural: ask what the word means. If *statistics* means the subject you studied, it *is*; if it means the figures, they *are*.

exercises.prompt: Over the last decade the company's overheads ___ increased dramatically.
exercises.explanation: overheads is one of the nouns that are normally plural, so the verb is plural.

exercises.statement: Phenomena such as sun spots have puzzled scientists for centuries.
exercises.explanation: Correct. phenomena (singular phenomenon) always takes a plural verb.

exercises.prompt: Modern linguistics ___ often said to have begun at the start of the 20th century.
exercises.explanation: linguistics is an uncountable noun ending in -s, so the verb is singular.

exercises.statement: Congratulations goes to Ricky Branch for his excellent exam results.
exercises.explanation: Congratulations go to Ricky Branch for his excellent exam results. congratulations is always plural.

exercises.prompt: Does each subject take a singular or a plural verb?

items.text: The news from the Middle East ...
The criteria used by the panel ...

exercises.prompt: I think the Senator's politics ___ extremely right-wing.
exercises.explanation: Here politics means political beliefs, so the verb is plural.

exercises.statement: The coastal surroundings of the village is particularly attractive.
exercises.explanation: The coastal surroundings of the village are particularly attractive. surroundings takes a plural verb.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order to make one sentence.
exercises.answer: Contact us by whatever means is most convenient for you.
exercises.explanation: means (= method) looks plural but takes a singular verb here.

exercises.prompt: Three hours ___ a long time to take on the homework.
exercises.explanation: The complement is a singular noun phrase (a long time), so the verb must be singular.

exercises.prompt: Only three metres ___ the runners in first and second places.
exercises.explanation: A phrase referring to a measurement usually prefers a singular verb.

exercises.prompt: About 50% of the houses ___ major repairs.
exercises.explanation: After a percentage the verb agrees with the noun closest to it - here houses.

exercises.prompt: An inflation rate of only 2% ___ a difference to exports.
exercises.explanation: Here the percentage is not the first noun, so the verb agrees with the main noun, rate.
